title: A Preregistered Audit of Dataset Contamination Controls in LLM-for-NetOps Benchmarks
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory audit (study_id = contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1) to evaluate whether a conservative detector suite (exact normalized token equality, fuzzy 5-gram overlap, provenance heuristics) would flag items in a reproducible 150-pair NetOps sample and whether applying a preregistered guarded exclusion policy would change validator-based success rates. The preregistered design fixed detectors and thresholds (fuzzy 5-gram high-confidence = 0.80), sampling (150 pairs), and the primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). The run used provenance-stable synthetic tasks and shared_initial_candidate semantics (independent_condition_generation = false), producing one shared generation per item reused across baseline and guarded episodes. No preregistered high-confidence contamination flags occurred; therefore no guarded exclusions or replacements were applied. Validator outcomes were identical (baseline_success = 150/150; guarded_success = 150/150), yielding a paired difference of 0.0 percentage points, paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729), and exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. We classify the preregistered primary estimand as degenerate/untestable for generation-level contamination under the executed semantics and provide an artifact-grounded reconciliation and concrete design changes (public provenance sampling, independent per-condition generation, full per-item overlap persistence, multi-model replication, paraphrase-robust detectors) to increase audit sensitivity. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle and summarized in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Motivation. Large language models (LLMs) are actively proposed as components of NetOps workflows—for intent translation, automated repair, and operational automation. Operational trust in such systems depends on evaluation validity: measured success must reflect genuine model capability rather than dataset contamination (benchmark items or templates present in model training data) or trivial templated structure. Methodological critiques emphasize contamination-aware evaluations combining deterministic fingerprinting, fuzzy n-gram overlap, provenance checks, and deterministic oracles.

Research question and contribution. We preregistered a confirmatory audit to answer: under a conservative, preregistered detector suite (exact-match + fuzzy 5-gram + provenance heuristics) and a deterministic guarded exclusion policy, how many high-confidence contamination flags arise in a reproducible 150-pair NetOps sample drawn from prespecified benchmark candidates, and how much does applying those controls change a validator-based success rate for a hosted LLM? The preregistration froze detectors, thresholds (fuzzy 5-gram high-confidence = 0.80), sample size (150 pairs), and the primary paired estimand. Our contributions are: (1) a fully preregistered confirmatory experiment executed end-to-end under the declared semantics; (2) exact, artifact-verified confirmatory statistics on Npairs = 150 with deterministic validator traces; and (3) an explicit preregistration–to–execution reconciliation that documents why the execution produced a degenerate null for generation-level contamination and prescribes artifact-anchored corrective design changes to increase audit sensitivity.
sections.related_work:
LLM-driven NetOps and verification. Prior systems and benchmark studies show that LLMs can synthesize device configuration artifacts from high-level intent and that coupling generation with deterministic verification (generate–validate–repair loops) reduces regressions compared with single-shot generation [https://openalex.org/W7157506260, https://openalex.org/W7163636922]. Deterministic validators based on header-space analysis and related formal methods provide precise reachability and policy checks well suited as oracles in these workflows [http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/summary?doi=10.1.1.300.8659, https://openalex.org/W2742515467].

Evaluation validity, contamination, and recommended defenses. Surveys and methodological analyses highlight persistent evaluation risks—dataset contamination, templating artifacts, and construct invalidity—and recommend layered defenses: normalized exact-match fingerprinting, fuzzy n-gram overlap, provenance timestamp heuristics, conservative exclusion/replacement policies, and human adjudication for borderline cases [https://openalex.org/W4404534210, https://openalex.org/W7166900660, https://openalex.org/W7140000903]. Our audit implements a conservative subset of these defenses (exact normalized equality; fuzzy 5-gram overlap with prespecified thresholds 0.50/0.65/0.80; provenance checks) and pairs them with a deterministic NetOps validator. Unlike large-scale leaderboards that focus on aggregate leaderboard ranking, we focus narrowly on whether those preregistered defenses, when applied with the declared execution semantics, change validator-measured success on a frozen confirmatory sample.
sections.methodology:
Preregistered design. The study (contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1) prespecified: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample size = 150 pairs; detectors = (1) exact normalized token equality, (2) fuzzy 5-gram shingle overlap with high-confidence threshold = 0.80 (sensitivity brackets at 0.65 and 0.50), and (3) provenance timestamp heuristics; guarded policy = deterministic exclusion and replacement for high-confidence flags subject to an embedding-similarity intent-preservation safeguard (minimal cosine ≥ 0.85). The analysis plan specified an exact McNemar two-sided test and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). All design choices and thresholds were fixed prior to execution.

Execution semantics and deterministic sampling. Execution used a deterministic task generator to produce provenance-stable synthetic confirmatory items (each labeled with a synthetic source identifier). The declared model was gpt-5-mini and the run used shared_initial_candidate semantics (independent_condition_generation = false): a single model generation per item could be reused across baseline and guarded episodes unless a high-confidence contamination flag triggered replacement. This reduced model calls (model_calls_used = 150 rather than the preregistered maximum of 300) and, crucially, mechanically collapses baseline vs guarded discordance when no exclusions occur. The verification oracle was a deterministic NetOps validator that performs explicit parsing and final-state checks; the validator returns a binary pass/fail plus deterministic traces for each episode.

Detector implementation and persistence policy. The detector suite implemented deterministic heuristics: exact normalized token equality; fuzzy 5-gram shingle overlap with preregistered high-confidence flag at overlap ≥ 0.80; and provenance timestamp comparisons against archive cutoffs. To reduce storage, the executed workflow persisted detailed per-item overlap outputs only when threshold crossings or replacements occurred. This persistence behavior was an explicit engineering tradeoff: when no high-confidence flags occur, the run archive therefore lacks a global per-item overlap table and prevents post-hoc sensitivity-curve visualization from the executed artifacts.

Guarded actions and analysis executor. The preregistered guarded policy excludes only high-confidence flagged items and deterministically replaces them with retemplated deterministic augmentations drawn from the same generator subject to the embedding-similarity safeguard. Confirmatory analysis used the registered executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 producing paired contingency counts, an exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The primary analysis follows the preregistered complete_pair_primary protocol.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. Execution completed the planned episodes (planned = 300 model-condition episodes corresponding to 150 item pairs). Because independent_condition_generation was false and no high-confidence exclusions occurred, the pipeline performed hosted-model generation calls for 150 shared_initial generations (model_calls_used = 150). The preregistered detectors produced zero high-confidence contamination flags in the executed sample; the contamination summary for this run is empty and no guarded replacements were applied.

Validator outcomes and confirmatory statistics. The deterministic validator returned pass for all baseline episodes (150/150) and for all guarded episodes (150/150). The paired contingency counts are n11 = 150, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) = 0.0 percentage points. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. These values are reported verbatim from the archived analysis outputs and reflect complete pair accounting (complete_pair_count = 150) and no missingness.

Representative diagnostics. Representative episode traces demonstrate reuse of the same generated candidate across baseline and guarded conditions when no exclusion applies: shared_initial_candidate was identical in paired episodes and parsed_command_count values in representative traces equal 4 (example cases), with validator reporting VALID_CONFIGURATION and explicit normalized_configuration in the validator trace. Deterministic reconciliation artifacts confirm stage accounting: completed_episode_count = 300, host-model call events = 150, and all internal consistency checks passed.
sections.discussion:
Why the primary estimand was untestable. The paired estimand was intended to detect changes when guarded exclusions remove contaminated generations. Under the executed semantics—provenance-stable synthetic sampling plus shared_initial_candidate semantics—baseline and guarded episodes reuse identical model outputs when no exclusions occur; thus the paired test is mechanically unable to observe generation-level discordance. The observed p-value and bootstrap CI correctly reflect concordant outcomes but are uninformative about contamination prevalence when generation variability is suppressed.

Artifact-grounded diagnosis and persistence tradeoffs. Two execution facts explain the degenerate null: (1) the confirmatory sample used provenance-stable synthetic tasks labeled as synthetic source items, and (2) independent_condition_generation was false, yielding a single shared generation per item that was reused across conditions unless an exclusion applied. Additionally, the executed persistence policy saved detailed fuzzy-overlap outputs only when threshold crossings or replacements occurred; because no high-confidence flags were observed, the repository lacks a full per-item overlap distribution. This storage-saving tradeoff materially reduces post-hoc interpretability and prevents reconstructing the fuzzy-overlap sensitivity curve from the archived artifacts.

Design sensitivity and recommended changes. Detecting modest paired differences (for example, a few percentage points) requires experiment semantics that permit generation variability across conditions and/or larger sample sizes and/or multi-model replication. Based on the deterministic reconciliation, we recommend concrete, artifact-anchored changes for future audits: (a) sample provenance-rich public items (the original preregistration targeted public OpenAlex benchmark sources) to expose potential pretraining-era overlaps; (b) set independent_condition_generation = true so baseline and guarded outputs are realized independently; (c) persist full per-item fuzzy-overlap scores for post-hoc sensitivity analysis and adjudication; (d) expand to multiple model instances and seeds to capture generation variability and stochastic leakage; and (e) integrate paraphrase-sensitive detectors (semantic similarity, paraphrase-resilient retrieval) and human adjudication for borderline flags. Each recommendation addresses explicit gaps revealed by the execution record (shared generation, empty contamination summary, and absent per-item overlaps).

Operational implications and external validity. Deterministic validators remain valuable: the NetOps validator provided precise functional-correctness traces enabling unambiguous scoring across archived episodes. However, auditors should not generalize the synthetic shared-generation null to web-crawled benchmarks. The present artifacts support only the narrow inference that, under deterministic synthetic sampling and shared-generation semantics, the preregistered conservative detectors produced no high-confidence flags and the guarded policy had no measurable effect. They do not inform contamination prevalence in web-sourced corpora nor detector performance against paraphrased memorization. Practical audits of public benchmarks should adopt the design changes above to enable nondegenerate hypothesis tests and provide interpretable sensitivity analyses.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-anchored paired audit of conservative contamination detectors for LLM-driven NetOps evaluation. In the reproducible 150-pair synthetic sample we observed zero preregistered high-confidence flags and identical validator pass rates (150/150 baseline, 150/150 guarded). The degenerate null outcome is supported by execution facts—provenance-stable synthetic sampling and shared_initial_candidate semantics—and therefore does not imply absence of contamination in web-sourced benchmarks. We provide an explicit preregistration–execution reconciliation, confirm deterministic reconciliation checks passed, and recommend concrete design changes (independent per-condition generation, full per-item overlap persistence, multi-model replication, paraphrase-robust detectors, and provenance-rich public sampling) to increase audit sensitivity. These recommendations follow directly from the archived execution and analysis artifacts. All execution, validator, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle and summarized in the Disclosure Statement below.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed under the autonomous-run preregistration contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1. Declared LLM: gpt-5-mini. Orchestration adapter and deterministic components included a hosted orchestration adapter, a deterministic task generator, and a deterministic NetOps validator. All generation prompts, model outputs, validator traces, sampling seeds, replacement rules, execution logs, and analysis artifacts produced by the autonomous pipeline are archived in the execution bundle. The autonomous system performed literature discovery, gap selection, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, simulated peer review, and revision after the autonomy lock; no manual human editing of technical content, analyses, references, figures, tables, captions, or this Disclosure Statement occurred after the autonomy lock. Exact immutable initial master-prompt reference (archived): provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).
limitations: Single-model execution (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize across other LLM families, sizes, or training corpora.

The executed sample used provenance-stable synthetic/deterministically generated tasks; absence of preregistered high-confidence flags here may not reflect contamination prevalence in real-world, web-crawled benchmarks (the preregistration had targeted public OpenAlex datasets).

Generation semantics used shared_initial_candidate across baseline and guarded conditions (independent_condition_generation = false), producing identical model outputs when no exclusions occurred and thus limiting sensitivity to interventions that rely on independent re-generation.

Contamination detection relied on preregistered conservative heuristics (exact match and fuzzy 5-gram overlap thresholds); subtler contamination patterns (paraphrased memorization, partial leakage) may escape these heuristics and require richer provenance, paraphrase-robust detectors, or human adjudication.

Passing the deterministic NetOps validator indicates satisfaction of the checked functional constraints but does not imply comprehensive production readiness or absence of semantic regressions outside the validator's scope.
